The visualization below compares American players’ win percentages at the US Open and the Australian Open from 2000 to 2025, offering insight into potential home-court advantage over time, and if it even exists. In the early 2000s, the Americans were playing very strongly at the US open, with win rates hovering above 60% and peaking near 70%. However, that advantage noticeably declined throughout the 2010s, with performance at both tournaments converging around the 40–50% mark as global competition intensified.

Interestingly, the past few years show a resurgence, particularly at the Australian Open, where American win percentages have climbed sharply again. Together, these trends suggest that while home-court advantage remains a factor in Grand Slam performance, there are many other factors that can influence whether a player wins a specific match. Players, no matter the nationality, have learned to adapt to changing environments and have had success winning anywhere in the world.
